chunk_map.heading: Hooks for must-happen, prompts for taste

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Checked every pronoun/demonstrative against the sequential-read bar. Chunk 1 line 5: "the agent has no say in whether it runs" -- "it" resolves to "hook", same sentence. Chunk 2 line 10: "Anything...stays in a prompt where the LLM weighs it" -- "it" resolves to "Anything", same sentence. Closest call: chunk 2 line 11, "This one runs on the screen. Watch the list come back rather than typing along." -- "This one" and "the list" point at the fenced Prompt block that sits immediately below, still inside the SAME chunk (raw lines 13-21 of the expanded view are the chunk-2 prompt), not a later slide. A projected slide renders as one simultaneous unit, so a same-chunk forward point is the rule-12 same-chunk carve-out's referent-resolution twin, not the banned late-named-referent shape ("before the three things get named" pointing at a LATER slide). Line 15's "The ones worth keeping" then resolves backward against that same prompt's output. No never-named or vague-with-full-history referent found anywhere in the file.

grep -inE 'the opening lecture|earlier|previously|prior lecture|the last (lecture|module|slide)|that (lecture|module)' over body lines 1-16 -> 0 hits. "someone else's article" (line 5) is a generic hypothetical, not a pointer to a specific file in this training. Nothing in the extraction (maintainer note: text pulled from what-packaging-is.md) left a residual cross-file callback -- checked directly, none survived.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -inE 'you (did|saw|wrote|built|ran|caught|made)' over body lines 1-16 -> 0 hits. No "the X you did/saw" construction naming a completed exercise beat anywhere in body -- nothing for this rule to strand.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -inE 'guess|predict|before you (watch|see|run)' over body lines 1-16 -> 0 hits. The prompt is delivered as a live watch-it-run demo ("Watch the list come back rather than typing along"), not a guess-then-reveal beat -- no predicted answer is stated anywhere for a later reveal to land after.

Chunk 0 is title-only (H1, no lede) -- the deck's standard title-slide shape, not a wait-state fragment. Chunk 1 carries two multi-clause bullets defining the hook primitive and its motivation. Chunk 2 carries two bullets, a live-run prompt widget, and a closing test line -- clearly self-carrying, not context-dependent filler.

Chunk 1 header "Hooks always fire" (line 3) is a true summary of its own content: line 5 states the hook fires unconditionally, line 6 restates via "Hooks don't forget." Chunk 2 header "Hooks for must-happen, prompts for taste" (line 8) covers its bullets' must-happen/hook vs taste/prompt split (lines 10-11). Closest call: the closing line (15) and the prompt widget extend into "which specific hooks are worth keeping," a corollary of the header's split rather than a contradiction of it -- the header still holds as the chunk's frame.

Checked every sub-item across both content chunks. 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' construction: grep -inE '^\s*(-\s*)?Not [A-Za-z]' over lines 1-16 -> 0 hits. Anaphora/epistrophe triples: none (no repeated sentence-opener run of three). Self-grading superlatives: grep -inE 'one of the most|most useful|most powerful' -> 0 hits; closest is "the LLM weighs it" / "a verifier against one failure is one hook" -- plain mechanism statements, no self-praise. Number + own retraction: only cardinal in body is "top five hooks" inside the prompt instruction to the model, not a claimed measurement the body itself hedges. Abstraction-noun stacks: none -- vocabulary stays concrete (verifier, pre-commit guard, session-start context loader, repo). Empty-leg verb triplets: none present.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -inE 'compendium|forcing function|\bbeat\b|\bmood\b|Connections|\bsurface\b' over body lines 1-16 -> 0 hits. "fires" (lines 5, 6) is the platform's own official hooks vocabulary (confirmed by the backing block's cc-hooks-docs source: "hook events...fire on every named event"), not authorial repo dialect -- an engineer reading Claude Code's own docs meets the same word. "verifier", "pre-commit guard", "session-start context loader" are ordinary engineering terms.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget -- bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -n '\*\*' over body lines 1-16 -> 2 hits: line 5 "A **hook**" (one word, defining the file's title term -- textbook handle) and line 10 "**Must happen goes in a hook**" (closest call: 6 words, a named-law/maxim restating the chunk-2 header's must-happen/taste split -- functions as the coined heuristic the rule wants surfaced, and it is the ONLY bold in its chunk, i.e. not the banned every-bullet-bolded monoculture -- bullet 2 in the same chunk carries no bold at all). Each chunk stays within the <=1-bolded-element budget; the "**Prompt** *(Claude Code)*" line is the fixed widget-frame label used identically on every Prompt widget across the corpus, not chunk-2 body prose competing for its emphasis budget.

rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -n 'hooks-always-fire' curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/*.md -> `learn-from-the-test.md:46:[Lecture: Hooks always fire](lectures/hooks-always-fire.md)`, sitting between the `reading-the-return` include (line 36, under `## Your mid-run worries hint at missing checks`) and the `fork-the-worktree` exercise include (line 48) -- exactly the maintainer block's claimed placement ("M5, after the reading-the-return opener, before fork-the-worktree"), confirmed live in the module body, not just asserted. rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Pure lecture file. Chunk 1 header "Hooks always fire" (line 3) and chunk 2 header "Hooks for must-happen, prompts for taste" (line 8) are both full declarative claims -- assertions about how the platform behaves and how the two mechanisms divide labor -- not topic labels or imperatives. Matches the lecture-heading claim requirement exactly; neither reads as a bare noun-phrase catalogue entry.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies -- three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Chunk 1's two bullets: definition (line 5) then motivation/why (line 6) -- second bullet adds a new idea (forgetfulness as the reason hooks exist), not a restatement of the first. Chunk 2's two bullets: the must-happen/taste split with concrete examples (line 10) then the repo-specificity setup for the live demo (line 11) -- distinct content, not doctrine repeated. Closest call: the closing line (15), "The ones worth keeping are tied to a specific file, convention, or failure mode in this repo, not a generic team-could-want-this" -- echoes bullet 2's "Your repo has demands that don't show up in someone else's article" in substance. Not cut as doctrine restatement (class a) because the maintainer block names this exact line as the load-bearing grading rubric applied to the live model output that just ran between bullet 2 and this line ("the trainer...reads the returned list against the closing line's test") -- it does real work interpreting fresh content, not re-announcing a point already closed. No self-referential pedagogy commentary (class b) and no koan restating the header (class c) found.
